title: Over a Jacobson base the relative dimension function agrees with the dimension of an integral subscheme
author: The Stacks Project Authors
work: Stacks Project, chapter chow.tex (Chow Homology and Chern Classes)
source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file chow.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261012
difficulty_reason: The lemma shows that over a Jacobson base whose closed points have dimension zero, the relative dimension function at the generic point of an integral subscheme, the dimension of that subscheme and the dimension of its local ring at a closed point all agree (statement lines 1457-1469, tag 02QK-adjacent). The proof uses the Jacobson property to reduce to closed points, expresses the dimension as a supremum of local ring dimensions, rewrites those as differences of dimension function values, and observes that at closed points the relative dimension function vanishes because the residue field extension is finite and the base point has dimension zero. The Jacobson reduction and the vanishing at closed points are the substance, so the claim is H2.
